words.alt: An anchor presents a storm report with a red bridge on the studio screen.
words.definition: The title that tells us the main news.
words.sentence: The headline tells us the main news.
words.cloze: The ___ is the title at the top of a news report.
words.tip: Make HEAD stronger. Link the two parts without adding a syllable.

words.alt: A reporter holds a microphone on dry ground above a flooded street.
words.definition: A person who gathers information and presents the news.
words.cloze: The ___ interviews people and presents the news.
words.tip: Make the middle syllable stronger. Keep the first and last syllables light.

words.alt: A resident in a yellow raincoat points to a fallen tree while a reporter listens.
words.definition: Someone who saw or experienced an event.
words.sentence: A witness saw the tree fall.
words.cloze: A ___ saw the tree fall and described what happened.
words.tip: Use two syllables. Make WIT stronger and keep the final s audible.

words.alt: River water covers a street and surrounds parked cars near a red bridge.
words.definition: Water covering land that is normally dry.
words.cloze: River water covered the road during the ___.
words.tip: Use one syllable. This word does not rhyme with food. Listen to the short vowel and final d.

words.alt: A fallen tree blocks a brick library entrance beside two broken windows.
words.definition: Harm to a building, object or place.
words.cloze: The broken windows show physical ___ to the library.
words.tip: Make the first syllable stronger. Keep the final sound; do not add a third syllable.

words.alt: A phone displays a flood warning symbol near a closed riverside path.
words.definition: A message about a possible danger or problem.
words.cloze: The council sent a ___ about danger near the river.
words.tip: Use two syllables. Finish with the nasal sound in -ing, without adding a separate g syllable.

words.alt: A rescue team helps two residents from a boat onto a dry landing.
words.definition: A team trained to help people in danger.
words.sentence: The rescue crew arrived by boat.
words.cloze: The ___ used a boat to bring people to dry ground.
words.tip: Say rescue in two syllables, then crew in one. Keep the words connected.

words.alt: A school gym contains camp beds, blankets, families and volunteers.
words.definition: A place where people can stay safely for a time.
words.cloze: Families stayed in a temporary ___ with beds and blankets.
words.tip: Start with the quiet sh sound. Make SHEL stronger and the last syllable lighter.

words.alt: Bottled water, food and blankets sit on a distribution table inside a gym.
words.definition: Useful things such as food, water and blankets.
words.cloze: Volunteers brought ___ such as water, food and blankets.
words.tip: Make the second syllable stronger. Keep the final voiced z sound.

words.alt: An editor checks a town council website and a printed official notice.
words.definition: The person, document or organization providing information.
words.sentence: Check the source of the news.
words.cloze: The editor checked the original ___ of the information.
words.tip: Use one syllable. Keep the final s audible without adding a vowel after it.

words.alt: A council spokesperson speaks into microphones at a public briefing.
words.definition: Something a person or organization says formally.
words.cloze: The council released an official ___ explaining its decision.
words.tip: Start directly with st, without adding a vowel before it. Make STATE stronger.

words.alt: Two photographs compare the same library before and after a storm.
words.definition: Information that supports or challenges a claim.
words.cloze: The before-and-after photos provide ___ of the damage.
words.tip: Use three syllables. Make the first one stronger and keep the others light.
